title: Tracks and editing on Focus; Getz projects
summary: Getz heard a track first; Sauter edited and effectively produced.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: We tried it again with the Boston Pops where I wrote--because there was no time for rehearsing--he couldn't hear what he was going to do, which on Focus we could--in both cases there was a track first and he could hear what he was going to do. He could learn the track.
You mean he didn't do it live in the studio? He did
Sometimes he did and sometimes he didn't. I would say it was fifty-fifty. That's the time that Scott-- what's his name-- (died in a car crash)
And another fellow; all these things happened at the same time (inaudible). Let's say it was fifty-fifty where he had the track--
(Side B of Tape 4 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 5.)

Let's say it was fifty-fifty where he had the tracks ahead of time. I know that he had the tracks ahead of time for the movie, because there is no problem, they can do that, but then he has to learn the stuff; how can he. He's got to hear it and a couple of the things he did right there and they were just as good, because he's that way.
Then came the editing; wow. That whole project took forever, and I had to do that. I really became the producer of that.
I can imagine there wasn't much--
